headings.title: SMTO-GML-0069 — SMTO changed only some of the emails you selected

html:
SMTO-GML-0069 — SMTO changed only some of the emails you selected

GUID: 842988b6-12ae-4a3a-9c24-7ef44cb8e650
Slug: gmail-compound-update-partial
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gmail-client-actions

What happened

  • Gmail accepted the change for some of the selected emails but not all of them, so SMTO stopped partway. Emails Gmail confirmed stay changed; for a few, SMTO may not know whether the change happened.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Read the result SMTO reported for this Task: how many emails were changed, failed, not attempted, or uncertain. Those numbers show how much of the work already happened before SMTO stopped.
  2. Open Gmail and look at some of the selected emails to see whether they are already archived, labeled, read or in Trash as you asked. For the uncertain emails, only Gmail itself shows whether the change went through.
  3. Ask SMTO to change only the emails that are still not right, by naming them or using a narrow search such as one sender or date. Repeating the whole request could redo or undo changes that already worked.
  4. If this was a reply and archive, don't ask for the reply again; ask only for the archiving that's left. The reply is sent before any archiving starts, so a new request could send a second copy.

What success looks like

  • In Gmail, every email you meant to change is in the expected state, and SMTO's last result reports no failed or uncertain emails.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the counts SMTO reported, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't repeat the whole request until you've checked which emails already changed.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Gmail bulk-action batch returned failed, unknown or unattempted message IDs (error_kind gmail_partial_update), so execute_snapshot stopped after keeping the acknowledged changes and did not replay the batch.

What this means

  • Per-item and per-batch receipts retain acknowledged changes, rejected messages, uncertain writes and unattempted work. The workflow stops rather than replaying a failed or ambiguous batch.

Why this can happen

  • Per-item and per-batch receipts retain acknowledged changes, rejected messages, uncertain writes and unattempted work. The workflow stops rather than replaying a failed or ambiguous batch.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the selected account, action arguments and operation reference; do not infer mailbox effects from the error alone.

How to fix it

  • Read the operation result counts (changed, failed, unknown, unattempted) and the invocation receipt's per-batch message ID lists, then compare the unknown IDs with their current Gmail labelIds. Request only the failed or unattempted IDs (and unknown ones after confirming their state) with an explicit narrower selection; do not replay the whole compound action.
  • Read the operation counts and saved receipts, then request only work whose prior outcome is known.

Retry and execution caution

  • Read the operation counts and saved receipts, then request only work whose prior outcome is known.

How to verify the fix

  • Confirmed, failed, unknown and unattempted outcomes are accounted for separately.

What not to do

  • Do not retry an entire compound action after a lost write acknowledgment.

Technical notes

  • Previously acknowledged changes remain confirmed; missing acknowledgments remain unknown. No automatic replay is authorized.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
